scenes.title: Why does product search sometimes pause?
scenes.label: A SHOPPER WAITS FOR RESULTS
scenes.voice: A shopper searches for running shoes. Results arrive late. Is the database slow, or is our Java service struggling with memory? Measure before guessing.
scenes.note: A slow search is a symptom. Identify the bottleneck.

cues.text: A shopper searches for running shoes.
Results arrive late.
Is the database slow, or is our Java
service struggling with memory?
Measure before guessing.

scenes.title: Search creates short-lived objects
scenes.label: HEAP AND REACHABILITY
scenes.voice: Search builds temporary product summaries. Many become unreachable after a response. Garbage collection reclaims them. Useful objects, such as a live catalogue cache, must remain.
scenes.note: Reachable is not the same as young. Age alone does not make garbage.

scenes.title: 2,000 ms search. 300 ms pause.
scenes.label: COMPARE SAME-SERVER EVIDENCE
scenes.voice: A two second search with a three hundred millisecond pause is not entirely a garbage collection problem. Compare database and inventory waits on the same timeline.
scenes.note: Illustrative intervals, not a measured performance result.

cues.text: A two second search with a three hundred
millisecond pause is not entirely a garbage collection
problem.
Compare database and inventory waits on the same
timeline.

scenes.title: Profile before changing the collector
scenes.label: REMOVE PROVEN REDUNDANT WORK
scenes.voice: Use Java Flight Recorder to find allocation hotspots. Remove repeated serialization and bound caches. Preserve correct product prices and availability, then repeat the same workload.
scenes.note: Do not change business results to reduce allocations.

cues.text: Use Java Flight Recorder to find allocation hotspots.
Remove repeated serialization and bound caches.

repeat the same workload.

scenes.title: Java 21 adds Generational ZGC
scenes.label: YOUNG AND OLD GENERATIONS
scenes.voice: Java twenty one adds Generational ZGC. It collects young objects separately from longer lived objects. This can reduce allocation stalls compared with non generational ZGC.
scenes.note: G1 also has generations. This feature extends ZGC.

cues.text: Java twenty one adds Generational ZGC.
It collects young objects separately from longer lived
objects.
This can reduce allocation stalls compared with non
generational ZGC.

scenes.title: Test the benefit. Keep correct results.
scenes.label: VALIDATE THE WHOLE SEARCH SERVICE
scenes.voice: Most ZGC work runs concurrently. Compare tail latency, errors, CPU, and memory before choosing it. This lesson teaches the method; it does not claim a measured speedup.
scenes.note: Less GC overhead is useful only if the full workload improves.
